To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nucleon electromagnetic form factor is dominated by the $\pi^\p\to N$ transition, and the coupling of the nucleon to $\pi^\p$, which is not yet observed in experiment, is estimated to be $\approx 1.2$ times the $\pi N$ coupling.

the IPE process, in which the pion is produced in the time-like photon region and then decays into the $e^+ e^-$ pair, is a unique laboratory for the study of the nucleon structure, and that the IPE cross section in the threshold region can be described by a simple formula with only two free parameters, the nucleon weak coupling constant $g_A$ and the pion-nucleon coupling constant $f$.
the nucleon weak form factors in the space-like domain can be determined from the experimental data on the inverse pion electro- and photoproduction in the time-like domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
studying nucleon structure in the sub- $N\bar{ N}$ -threshold region of the time-like virtual photon mass.

the study of the electromagnetic and weak structure of the proton and the neutron, and with the search for new hadronic states in the region of the sub-threshold $\pi N$-scattering, using the process $\pi N \to e^+ e^- N$, in which the nucleon is in the initial state.

the study of the electromagnetic and weak structure of hadrons in the sub-$\bar{N}N$-threshold region of the virtual photon ``mass'' $\l$ and the investigation of the properties of the new hadronic state $\pi^\ast$.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nucleon electromagnetic form factors in the space-like and time-like regions are determined in a practically model-independent way, and that a new state of $\pi^\p$, which is a radial excitation of the pion, is found and the coupling constant is estimated.
the nucleon weak electromagnetic structure in the region of the first radial excitaion of pion, as well as the existence of this excitation, is established.

the results of the present analysis of IPE data at low energies provide a strong support for the existence of the $\pi^\p\, N$-channel, and, hence, for a new state $\pi^\pi$ with the mass $M=0.5-0.8$ GeV and with the width $\Gamma=200-400$ MeV, which can be considered as the first radial excitaion of pion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleon weak form factor $F_{2W}$ in the space-like domain is determined with an accuracy of about 20% in the range 0.1-0.3 $({\rm GeV}/c)^2$.
the IPE process at low energies is a very useful and promising tool for studying the nucleon weak and electromagnetic structure.
we have obtained a new and very interesting result: a new state of $\pi$-meson in the range 600-800 MeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the $\pi^\p\,N$ coupling is very small, which is a strong indication that this new state is not a resonance.

the IPE process at low energies is very promising for investigating hadron structure, and the experimental data obtained at the VEPP-3, VEPP-4, VEPP-2000 and VEPP-4M colliders in Novosibirsk and at the DA$\Phi$NE collider in Frascati are sufficient for such investigations.
, at low energies, the nucleon weak form factor can be extracted with an accuracy of about 10% from the IPE data.
